newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh plane was in good condition - official.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh plane was in good condition - official.

text.p: Kazakhstan's state airline said on Wednesday the Ilyushin Il-76TD cargo plane which collided with a Saudi Arabian airliner in mid-air near New Delhi, killing 351 people, had been in good technical condition.
"We're only at the beginning of the investigation. We have very few details," Ildus Nazmutdinov, vice-president of Kazakhstan National Airways (KazAir), told Reuters in the Kazakh capital Almaty.
"The aircraft was in good technical condition," he said.
Nazmutdinov spoke just before he and other KazAir representatives were due to leave for New Delhi to meet Indian officials.
He said there were 27 passengers, including one child, on board -- not 28 as reported earlier -- and 10 crew members.
The KazAir plane collided with the Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747 on Tuesday two hours and 10 minutes after taking off from Chimkent in southern Kazakhstan, said Nazmutdinov.
KazAir has been dogged by financial problems and was formally closed down in August after being criticised by the government for falling safety standards.
The crashed plane had been chartered from KazAir by a firm in the Kyrgyzstan capital Bishkek, said a Kazakh transport official.
Many of the passengers were Kyrgyzstan nationals while the crew came from Chimkent, said Nazmutdinov.
